messages:
Maria Chen: Quick thread — thinking through service boundary contracts: should we standardize on gRPC+protobuf for internal platform services, or stick with REST/JSON for maximum interoperability? Pros/cons on rollout UX, telemetry, quotas?
Alex Rivera: +1 to weighing SDK ergonomics. gRPC gives typed contracts and faster payloads, but node teams keep hitting native gRPC pain. :grimacing:
Cheng Wu: gRPC + proto is nice for quota enforcement and streaming telemetry (we can attach metadata easily). But schema evolution and one-time migrations have bitten us before.
Devon Patel: From the console side, JSON is way easier to debug in browser devtools. We also rely on wildcard routes and simple REST semantics for some dashboards.
Samir Joshi: Happy to prototype a hybrid: core control plane services gRPC internally, gateway exposes REST for UI & webhooks. Gateway would translate and enforce quotas/headers.
Maria Chen: That’s similar to what some teams do. Concern: translation layer becomes a compatibility choke point and hides errors. How do we keep tracing and distributed telemetry end-to-end across the translation?
Cheng Wu: Use context propagation headers (traceparent) and map gRPC metadata <-> HTTP headers. Also emit a cross-system request_id at gateway entry so logs align.
Alex Rivera: Example proto vs REST payload:

```proto
// example service.proto
service RouteService {
  rpc CreateRoute(CreateRouteRequest) returns (Route) {}
}
message CreateRouteRequest {
  string name = 1;
  repeated string tags = 2;
}
```

vs

```json
{ "name": "a", "tags": ["x","y"] }
```

Alex Rivera: Protos guard types (no accidental ints-as-strings) but adds compile step and generator headaches for multiple languages.
Devon Patel: Also think about rollout UX: when we change contract, can frontend teams feature-flag new fields? With REST they can be tolerant. With proto strict typing we need server-side defaulting and versioned RPCs.
Samir Joshi: Suggestion: adopt strict proto for service-to-service; require server-side backward compat by following proto3 optional fields + defaulting, and add a lightweight REST shim that keeps the old shape for UI consumers. Document migration steps in the API changelog.
Maria Chen: Quotas & routing policy: if we have mixed transports, billing/quotas should be applied at gateway boundary (single enforcement point). But for Dedicated infra we sometimes route directly to gRPC endpoints — how do we ensure consistent quota accounting?
Cheng Wu: Emit a unified telemetry event at ingress (gateway or edge router) with metadata: client_id, routing_policy, model_variant. Quota service should consume those events rather than pulling from many services.
Devon Patel: UX note: console needs per-route latency/cost breakdowns. If gateway hides which model variant served a request, we lose observability. So shims must preserve model headers and KV cache tags.
Alex Rivera: Ops point: graceful degradation — if gRPC path fails, gateway could fallback to a REST-compatible handler backed by a different model variant. Need clear fallback semantics in the routing policy config.
Samir Joshi: Can we express fallback policies declaratively? e.g.,

```yaml
routing:
  primary: endpoint-grpc://routerA
  fallback: endpoint-rest://legacyB
  conditions:
    - latency > 300ms
    - capacity < 20%
```

Samir Joshi: If gateway enforces that, we get consistent behavior across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
Maria Chen: Sounds good. Action items: 1) prototype a small shim that preserves tracing/headers and supports fallback; 2) doc template for contract changes (proto->rest mapping); 3) telemetry event spec for ingress quotas.
Alex Rivera: I'll volunteer to do the shim POC (Node + Envoy). @Cheng can you draft the telemetry schema? @Devon can you list the UI fields that must survive translation?
Cheng Wu: On it — will put a strawman telemetry JSON in #eng-platform later today.
Devon Patel: Will pull console requirements and add to the doc. Also we should add a migration checklist for frontend teams.
deploy-bot: deploy started: shim-poc branch -> staging (build 87c4)
Maria Chen: thanks everyone. If shim works we can iterate on stricter proto adoption later. :thumbsup:
